domain: Medical AI agents and multimodal clinical reasoning

clusters.label: Agentic Clinical Reasoning with Tool Use
clusters.description: Research on autonomous medical AI agents that iteratively invoke external biomedical tools, gather evidence, and present transparent reasoning to clinicians or patients, while evaluating trust, safety, and alignment.
clusters.rationale: All five papers focus on autonomous, tool‑enabled AI agents for medical decision making, covering trust assessment, reinforcement‑learning training, patient‑facing benchmarks, human intervention points, and preference‑elicitation prompting, which together define the sub‑field of agentic clinical reasoning with tool use.

clusters.label: Agentic Multimodal Clinical Decision Support
clusters.description: Research focused on building autonomous, tool‑using AI agents that ingest and fuse heterogeneous clinical data (text, imaging, sensor streams, knowledge graphs) to augment and guide clinical reasoning across diverse medical domains.
dominant_methods: Tool‑using agentic AI frameworks (e.g., ReAct, AutoGPT)
Large language model prompting for clinical reasoning
Explainable / causal AI for safety alerts
clusters.rationale: All six papers describe autonomous or semi‑autonomous AI systems that combine multiple data modalities (e.g., traditional medicine texts, pathology slides, imaging, intra‑operative sensor streams) and employ agentic architectures or knowledge‑graph‑driven pipelines to provide decision support, safety monitoring, or reasoning assistance, indicating a shared technical direction.

clusters.label: Agentic Multimodal 3D Medical Reasoning
clusters.description: Research focused on building autonomous AI agents that can ingest, represent, and reason over three-dimensional medical data (e.g., volumetric imaging, surgical video) together with textual and procedural knowledge, enabling end‑to‑end clinical decision support, training, and workflow integration.
dominant_methods: Self‑evolving reinforcement learning in clinical environments
clusters.rationale: All four papers converge on the challenge of creating AI agents that can handle native 3D medical representations (volumetric scans, surgical video) and integrate them with language‑based reasoning, tool use, and interactive training, highlighting methods such as volumetric foundation models, agentic planning, and RAG.

clusters.label: Agentic Multimodal Clinical Reasoning
clusters.description: Research that equips medical AI agents with the ability to jointly process heterogeneous clinical data (e.g., EHR, radiology images, ultrasound) and perform multi‑hop, evidence‑guided reasoning using retrieval, graph structures, and reinforcement‑learning policies.
dominant_methods: Dynamic hypergraph construction for multimodal data
Reinforcement learning agents for path navigation
Causal reinforcement learning for evidence selection
Dual‑LLM architecture separating reasoning from prediction
Agentic invoke‑and‑reason framework with sequential RL
clusters.rationale: All three papers propose agentic or reinforcement‑learning driven frameworks that integrate multimodal clinical inputs (EHR, X‑ray, ultrasound) via retrieval or graph‑based structures to enable multi‑step diagnostic reasoning, indicating a coherent sub‑field of agentic multimodal clinical reasoning.

clusters.label: Agentic Multimodal Clinical Reasoning
clusters.description: Research on building medical AI agents that combine multimodal perception, tool use, and long‑term memory to perform step‑wise, evidence‑grounded clinical reasoning across text, images, and time‑series data.
clusters.rationale: All eight papers propose or evaluate medical AI agents that integrate multimodal inputs (text, images, time‑series) with tool‑use, reinforcement‑learning based policy training, and memory mechanisms to enable continuous, evidence‑driven clinical reasoning. The recurring technical motifs—agentic frameworks, multimodal LLMs, structured memory, and preference‑based RL—justify a unified taxonomy label focused on agentic multimodal clinical reasoning.

clusters.label: Multi-Agent Explainable Clinical Reasoning
clusters.description: Research focused on building cooperative multi‑agent architectures that provide safe, verifiable and interpretable decision support for clinical tasks involving multimodal data such as medical images and time‑series measurements.
dominant_methods: Hierarchical explainability (temporal Shapley, attention, gradient attribution)
Ensemble vision models for robust imaging diagnosis
clusters.rationale: All three papers propose multi‑agent systems that combine specialized AI components (vision ensembles, statistical agents, temporal transformers) with explicit uncertainty quantification and layered explanations, targeting trustworthy clinical reasoning over multimodal inputs.

clusters.label: Multimodal Diagnostic Reasoning in Clinical AI
clusters.description: Research that develops, evaluates, and benchmarks large multimodal models capable of integrating textual patient data, medical images, and longitudinal evidence to generate accurate, evidence‑grounded clinical diagnoses and reasoning.
dominant_methods: Recursive/agentic reasoning frameworks with evidence graphs
Benchmark construction from curated case reports
Shortcut mitigation via modality ablation and route audits
clusters.rationale: All five papers address the challenge of enabling AI agents to reason over heterogeneous clinical evidence (text, images, longitudinal data) and produce diagnostically sound outputs. They converge on multimodal model architectures, structured prompting, recursive reasoning, and rigorous benchmark design to assess true clinical reasoning rather than shortcut exploitation.

clusters.label: Tool-Augmented Multimodal Clinical Reasoning
clusters.description: Research focused on building autonomous agents that jointly process medical images, text, and other health data, using external tools (e.g., retrieval, knowledge graphs, visual grounding) to acquire, verify, and integrate evidence for interpretable clinical decision‑making.
clusters.rationale: All three papers propose agentic systems that combine visual and textual modalities, employ external tools (retrieval, knowledge graphs, visual grounding) to gather and verify evidence, and output diagnoses or reports with explicit reasoning traces, indicating a shared technical direction toward tool‑augmented multimodal clinical reasoning.
